title: Role of Livestock in National Economy
definition: Animal husbandry is an integral component of Indian agriculture supporting the livelihood of more than two-thirds of the rural population, providing nutrient-rich food products, draught power, organic manure, fuel, and acting as living capital and insurance against crop failure.

sections.heading: Importance in Rural Economy
items: Integral part of agricultural production: India accounts for ~57.3% of the world's buffalo population, 14.7% of cattle, and 20.4% of small ruminants.
Employment generation: Engages ~20.5 million workers in animal farming; agriculture overall engages ~57% of total working population and 73% of rural labour force.
Women empowerment: Over three-fourths of labour demand in livestock production is met by women, reaching ~90% in Punjab and Haryana.

Nutritional security: Contributes significantly to milk and egg availability; per capita milk availability stands at 283 g/day (vs. ICMR recommendation of 300 g/day) and egg availability at 55 eggs/year.
Income and power generation: Generates around 16% of farmer income, provides draught/draft power for ploughing, threshing, water harvesting, and transportation.
Soil fertility and by-products: Supplies dung, urine, and organic manure; provides feedstock for gobar gas plants; yields slaughterhouse by-products and medicinal inputs (serum, vaccines).

sections.heading: Production of Major Livestock Products (2011-12)
items: Milk: 127.9 million tonnes (annual growth rate ~5%).
Eggs: 66.45 billion numbers.
Wool: 44.73 million kg.
Meat: 5.5 million tonnes (growth rate ~13%).
Fish: 86.66 lakh tonnes (33.71 lakh tonnes marine, 52.95 lakh tonnes inland).

sections.heading: Major Challenges in Animal Husbandry
items: Low animal productivity: Indian cattle average annual milk yield is 1,172 kg (~50% of global average).
Feed and fodder deficit: Deficit of 11% dry fodder, 35% green fodder, and 28% concentrate feed; only 5% of cropped area grows fodder.
Breeding and AI constraints: Poor conception rates and limited AI infrastructure; crossbred population remains low (16.6% in cattle, 21.5% in pigs, 5.2% in sheep).
Disease outbreaks: Recurrent losses due to FMD, BQ, PPR, and avian influenza.

Inadequate infrastructure and financial support: Insufficient public expenditure (~12% of agri-budget), low formal credit share (<4%), inadequate registered slaughterhouses, and only 6% livestock insurance coverage.

title: Reproduction in Farm Animals and Poultry
definition: The physiological processes, anatomical structures, and management practices involved in gametogenesis, mating, fertilization, gestation, and artificial insemination across domestic livestock and avian species.

sections.heading: Male Reproductive System (Mammals)
items: Testes: Paired ovoid organs located in scrotum, site of spermatogenesis and testosterone synthesis.
Epididymis: Coiled tube for sperm maturation, storage, and transport.

Accessory Glands: Vesicular glands (nourishment/transport medium), Prostate gland (milky fluid conferring substance and nutrients), and Bulbourethral/Cowper's glands (neutralizes urinary acid residues).
Penis Types: Vascular penis (stallion, depends on engorgement without sigmoid flexure); Fibroelastic penis (bull, ram, boar, contains S-shaped sigmoid flexure when relaxed).

sections.heading: Female Reproductive System (Mammals)
items: Ovaries: Produce ova, estrogen (follicles), and progesterone (corpus luteum).
Oviducts (Fallopian tubes): Site of fertilization; infundibulum receives ovulated ova.
Uterus: Site of embryo incubation and development; varies from long horns (sow) to short horns (mare).
Cervix and Vagina: Cervix forms fibrous barrier and seals uterus during pregnancy; vagina acts as copulatory organ and birth canal.

sections.heading: Reproductive Parameters of Domestic Animals
items: Cow: Puberty at 24-36 months; Estrus cycle 21 days; Ovulation 10-14 hrs after heat; Gestation 280±5 days; Normal temp 99.5-101.5°F.
Buffalo: Puberty at 36-42 months; Estrus cycle 21 days; Ovulation 10-14 hrs after heat; Gestation 310±5 days; Normal temp 99-102°F.
Ewe: Puberty at 6-12 months; Estrus cycle 17 days; Ovulation at end of heat; Gestation 155 days; Normal temp 102°F.
Goat: Puberty at 6-12 months; Estrus cycle 18-20 days; Ovulation at end of heat; Gestation 155 days; Normal temp 103-104°F.
Sow: Puberty at 5-8 months; Estrus cycle 21 days; Ovulation 35 hrs after heat onset; Gestation 115 days; Normal temp 102°F.

sections.heading: Avian Reproductive Anatomy & Artificial Insemination
items: Male poultry: Testes located internally along backbone; rudimentary copulatory phallus engorges with lymph.

Female poultry: Only left ovary and oviduct are functional; oviduct comprises Infundibulum (fertilization site), Magnum (thick albumen secretion), Isthmus (shell membranes), Uterus (thin white, shell, pigment), and Vagina.
Poultry AI: Fresh diluted semen (normal saline 1:2) used within 1 hour; dose is 0.03 ml/hen; administered after 3:00 PM when oviposition is completed.

title: Housing Principles and Space Requirements for Livestock and Poultry
definition: Guidelines and space specifications required to provide safe, comfortable, properly ventilated, and cost-effective shelter that maximizes growth, health, and productive performance.

sections.heading: Core Principles of Animal Housing
items: Protection: Shield animals from heat, cold, rain, mud, and predatory intrusion.
Feeding & Watering: Standard manger space of 50 cm/head; provide adequate water troughs (average need is 10 litres water/100 kg live weight/day).
Ventilation & Comfort: Promote free airflow to dissipate carbon dioxide and ammonia; provide clean, non-slippery resting areas.

sections.heading: Space Requirements for Livestock
items: Bulls: 12.0 m² covered area, 120.0 m² open yard.
Cows: 3.5 m² covered area, 7.0 m² open yard.
Down Calves: 4.0 m² covered area, 8.0 m² open yard.
Young Calves: 1.0 m² covered area, 1.5 m² open yard.
Older Calves: 2.0 m² covered area, 4.0 m² open yard.
Ewe / Nanny: 1.0 - 2.0 m² covered area.
Boar: 6.0 - 7.0 m² covered area, 8.8 - 12.0 m² open yard.
Farrowing Sow: 7.0 - 9.0 m² covered area, 8.8 - 12.0 m² open yard.

sections.heading: Poultry Housing Systems
items: Free-range / Extensive: Traditional system requiring extensive open ground.
Semi-intensive: Fixed housing with 20-30 square yards run space per bird.
Folding Unit: Portable units holding ~25 birds (1 sq. ft house, 3 sq. ft run per bird), moved daily.
Battery Cage System: Cages (14 x 16 inches, 17 inches high) with sloping mesh floor and droppings tray; space saving but holds only unfertilized pullet production.
Deep Litter System: Litter (straw/sawdust) 8-12 inches deep; builds built-up dry compost generating Animal Protein Factor and vitamin B2 (riboflavin); stocking up to 250 birds per pen.

title: Management of Calves, Growing Heifers and Milch Animals
definition: Standard operating practices and nutritional regimens for dairy cattle across lifecycle stages, from neonatal calf care to heifer rearing and lactating cow management.

sections.heading: Newborn Calf Management & Colostrum Feeding
items: Neonatal care: Clean nostrils, stimulate respiration, cut umbilical cord 3 cm from body, treat stump with tincture of iodine.
Colostrum feeding: Administer colostrum within 2 hours of birth at 10% of body weight (superior nutrition, high vitamins A/D/E, imparts passive immunity and acts as laxative for meconium).
Calf Starter: Formulated concentrate (16% DCP, 70% TDN, ~20% quality protein) fed from day 10 onward.
Milk Replacer: Reconstituted warm liquid diet containing 50% spray-dried skim milk, 12% fat, and 22% protein.

sections.heading: Growing Heifer Management
items: Housing: Provide 2 m² covered space and 4 m² open yard per heifer from 6 months of age.
Steaming-up: Supplementary concentrate feeding (1.5 kg/day of 18% DCP, 65-70% TDN) during the last trimester of pregnancy to support foetal growth, mammary development, and future milk yields.
Challenge feeding: Increasing concentrate allowance by 500 g daily during the last 15 days before calving to acclimate the digestive tract.
Breeding benchmarks: Breed Indian heifers at 2-3 years and crossbred heifers at 1-2 years, when they attain 60% of mature body weight.

sections.heading: Lactating/Milch Cow Care & Feeding
items: Feeding rules: Indigenous cows receive 1 kg concentrate (16% DCP) per 2.5-3.0 kg milk; crossbreds/buffaloes receive 1 kg per 2.0-2.5 kg milk over maintenance allowance.
Milking hygiene: Wash udders with antiseptic solution, groom 2 hours prior to milking, follow a strict 12-hour or 8-hour schedule.
Dry Period: Provide a dry period of 60 days before the next expected calving date.

title: Management of Sheep, Goat and Swine
definition: Husbandry, nutritional strategies, and reproductive management protocols for sheep, goats, and domestic swine.

sections.heading: Sheep and Goat Terminology & Characteristics
items: Sheep (Ovis aries, 2n=54): Castrated male is wether/wedder; Mating is tupping; Parturition is lambing; Feeding style is grazing.
Goat (Capra hircus, 2n=60): Castrated male is wether; Mating is serving; Parturition is kidding; Meat is chevon; Feeding style is browsing.

sections.heading: Nutritional Practices for Small Ruminants
items: Flushing ewes: Elevating dietary nutrition 2-3 weeks before breeding season (May in India) to stimulate ovarian activity, increase ovulation, and boost twinning rates.
Creep feed for kids: 22% protein ration fed at 50-100 g/kid/day from 1 month to 2-3 months of age to support fast pre-weaning weight gains.
Colostrum in kids: Fed at 100 ml per kg body weight; may be preserved with 1-1.5% propionic acid.

sections.heading: Swine Production and Husbandry
items: Breeding biology: Gestation period is ~114 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days); heat duration 2-3 days; best bred on first day (gilts) or second day (sows).
Feed conversion: High dressing percentage (65-80%) and exceptional feed conversion ratio compared to large ruminants.
Wallow requirement: Essential due to very few functional sweat glands in pigs; masonry wallows with drainage prevent heat stress.

title: Incubation, Hatching, Brooding, and Flock Management
definition: Technical parameters governing artificial incubation of hatching eggs, brooding environment controls, and housing practices for growers, broilers, and commercial laying flocks.

sections.heading: Principles of Incubation
items: Critical physical factors: Temperature, relative humidity, adequate ventilation (O2 and CO2 levels), position (broad end up), and regular turning of eggs.
Candling: Carried out during transfer from setter to hatcher to eliminate unfertilized eggs and dead embryos.

sections.heading: Brooding Environmental Standards
items: Temperature schedule: 95°F (35°C) during week 1, reduced by 5°F each week until reaching 70°F (21.1°C).
Brooder space: 7 to 10 sq inches (45-65 cm²) per chick under hovers; a 1.8 m hover holds 500 chicks.
Hover guard: Placed 1.05 to 1.50 m from the hover edge during the first week to keep chicks near warmth.

sections.heading: Management Pointers for High Egg Production
items: Lighting: Constant 16 hours of light per day (never exceed 17 hours; never decrease photoperiod during lay).
Space allowance (Layers 17-76 wks): Deep litter requires 2.0 sq. ft/bird; Cages require 0.8 sq. ft/bird.
Starvation risks: 6 hours without feed causes immediate drop in lay; 12 hours causes molt of wing feathers; water deprivation rapidly induces forced molting.
Cannibalism prevention: Implement precision debeaking, provide adequate feeder/water space, avoid excessive light intensity, and maintain proper stocking density.

title: Breeds of Livestock and Poultry
definition: Morphological classification, geographic origins, and economic utility categories of indigenous and exotic breeds of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats, swine, and chickens.

sections.heading: Indigenous and Exotic Cattle Breeds
items: Milch Breeds: Gir, Sahiwal, Red Sindhi, Tharparkar, Rathi.
Draught Breeds: Amritmahal, Hallikar, Kangayam, Khillari, Bargur, Nagori, Bachaur, Kenkatha, Malvi, Siri, Vechur.
Dual-Purpose Breeds: Hariana, Ongole, Deoni, Gaolao, Kankrej, Mewati, Krishna Valley.
Exotic Breeds: Holstein Friesian (Holland), Jersey (England), Brown Swiss (Switzerland), Guernsey (France).
Crossbred Cattle: Karan-Swiss (Brown Swiss × Sahiwal), Karan-Fries (HF × Tharparkar), Frieswal (HF × Sahiwal), Sunandini (Brown Swiss × Local).

sections.heading: Buffalo Breeds
items: Riverine Breeds: Murrah (premier dairy breed, curled horns), Nili-Ravi, Surti, Mehsana, Jaffarabadi, Bhadawari (high milk fat).
Swamp Breeds: Found mainly in Assam and parts of Tamil Nadu (e.g., Toda buffaloes).

sections.heading: Goat and Sheep Breeds
items: Jamunapari Goat: Tall, long-legged, Roman nose ('parrot mouth' appearance), large pendulous ears; dual-purpose (milk & meat).
Other Indian Goats: Barbari, Beetal, Sirohi, Black Bengal (high prolificacy/skin quality), Chegu/Changthangi (pashmina producers).
Indian Sheep: Chokla (fine carpet wool), Magra, Nali, Marwari, Deccani, Nellore (mutton), Mandya, Nilgiri.

sections.heading: Swine and Poultry Breeds
items: Swine: Large White Yorkshire (England), Middle White Yorkshire, Landrace (Switzerland), Berkshire, Hampshire, T&D crossbred.
Poultry Classes: American (Rhode Island Red, Plymouth Rock), Mediterranean (White Leghorn), English (Australorp, Cornish, Sussex), Asiatic (Brahma, Cochin).
Indigenous Chicken: Aseel (game bird/fighting), Kadaknath (melanic/black flesh), Naked Neck, Nicobari.

source: Livestock & Poultry Management, Chapter 7 & Appendix, pp. 39-46, 94-107

title: Digestion in Livestock and Poultry
definition: The physiological, mechanical, and microbial mechanisms responsible for the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids within ruminant stomachs and monogastric avian digestive tracts.

sections.heading: Ruminant Stomach Compartments
items: Rumen: Largest compartment, active microbial fermentation vat; absorbs VFAs; pH buffered between 6.2 and 6.8 by saliva (60-70 L/day).
Reticulum: Honeycomb lining; coordinates regurgitation and cud chewing; functions in conjunction with rumen.
Omasum: Manyplies structure with leaf-like tissue folds; functions in water and mineral reabsorption.
Abomasum: 'True stomach' with acid (HCl) and pepsin/enzyme secretions, comparable to monogastric stomachs.

sections.heading: Microbial Fermentation & By-products
items: Carbohydrate digestion: Cellulose, hemicellulose, and starch are converted into volatile fatty acids (VFAs: Acetic, Propionic, and Butyric acids), providing 50-70% of energy.
Fiber vs Grain diet: High-fiber roughage produces 60-70% acetic acid; high-grain concentrates increase propionic acid up to 40% (lowering milk fat percentage).
Protein synthesis: Rumen microflora hydrolyze feed proteins and non-protein nitrogen (NPN such as urea) into ammonia to assemble microbial crude protein.
Vitamin synthesis: Microorganisms synthesize all B-complex vitamins and Vitamin K in quantities sufficient for maintenance.

sections.heading: Calf Stomach Development
items: Esophageal groove reflex directs sucked milk directly past the undeveloped rumen/reticulum into the abomasum.
Functional rumen development begins at 3-4 weeks and matures to adult capacity by ~3 months of age.

title: Classification of Feedstuffs, Proximate Principles, and Ration Formulation
definition: Classification of animal feedstuffs into roughages, concentrates, supplements, and additives, along with proximate chemical analysis and ration computation principles.

sections.heading: Classification of Feedstuffs
items: Roughages: >18% Crude Fibre (CF) and <60% TDN; divided into Green/Succulent (60-90% moisture: berseem, lucerne, maize, silage) and Dry roughages (10-15% moisture: straw, stover, hay).
Concentrates: <18% CF and >60% TDN; categorized into Carbonaceous/Energy-rich (maize, barley, oats, wheat bran) and Protein-rich (groundnut cake, soybean meal, fish meal).

sections.heading: Weende Proximate Analysis
items: Moisture: Determined by drying at 100°C; non-moisture portion represents Dry Matter (DM).
Crude Protein (CP): Measured via Kjeldahl nitrogen determination multiplied by 6.25 (assuming 16% N in protein).
Crude Fibre (CF): Insoluble carbohydrate fraction remaining after boiling in weak acid and alkali.
Ether Extract (EE): Neutral fats, lipids, and pigments extracted with petroleum ether.
Total Ash: Inorganic mineral fraction remaining after complete incineration at 600°C.
Nitrogen-Free Extract (NFE): Soluble starches and sugars calculated by difference [100 - (Moisture + CP + CF + EE + Ash)].

sections.heading: Dairy Cattle Feeding Standards
items: Dry matter intake: 2.5% body weight for dry cows; 3.0% for lactating dairy cows.
Ration distribution: 2/3 of total DM from roughages (2/3 dry fodder + 1/3 green fodder) and 1/3 DM from concentrates.
Maintenance allowance: 1.0 - 1.5 kg concentrate for desi cows; 1.5 - 2.0 kg for crossbred cows and buffaloes.
Production allowance: 1 kg concentrate per 2.5-3 kg cow milk (or per 2.0-2.5 kg buffalo milk).

title: Diseases of Livestock and Poultry, Prevention and Vaccination Schedules
definition: Etiology, clinical manifestations, prevention, and compulsory vaccination protocols for major viral, bacterial, parasitic, and metabolic diseases affecting farm animals and poultry.

sections.heading: Major Bacterial Diseases
items: Black Quarter (BQ, Clostridium chauvoei): Emphysematous hot, painful swellings over heavy muscles (loins/buttocks) that crackle on pressure, high fever; annual pre-monsoon vaccination in stock >6 months.
Haemorrhagic Septicaemia (HS, Pasteurella multocida): Throat oedema, severe dyspnoea, grunting, high mortality (up to 80%); pre-monsoon annual vaccination.
Anthrax (Bacillus anthracis): Sudden death, blood oozing from natural orifices, uncoagulated blood; strictly never open carcass; annual vaccination in endemic zones.
Brucellosis (Brucella abortus): Contagious abortion in late pregnancy (>5th month); zoonotic; single lifetime calfhood vaccination of female calves between 4-8 months.
Bovine Tuberculosis & Johne's Disease: Chronic wasting diseases causing emaciation and persistent diarrhoea; incurables; culled upon positive testing.

sections.heading: Viral and Metabolic Diseases
items: Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD): Vesicles in mouth and interdigital cleft, heavy drop in milk; biannual vaccination (every 6 months).

Rabies: Transmitted through bites of rabid carnivores; symptoms include hyper-excitability, salivation, bellowing, paralysis, inevitable death; post-bite vaccination regimen (days 0, 4, 7, 14, 28, 90).
Milk Fever: Hypocalcaemia occurring within 72 hours of calving; caused by sudden calcium drain into colostrum; causes sternal recumbency, paresis, and coma.
Ketosis (Acetonemia): Hypoglycaemia and ketone body accumulation 10-60 days postpartum; sweetish acetone odor in breath and milk.

sections.heading: Poultry Vaccination Schedule
items: Day 0: Marek's Disease Vaccine (HVT) — 0.2 ml subcutaneous (S/C).
1st Week: Ranikhet Disease Vaccine (RDVF / F-strain) — Eye/nasal drop (O/N).
2nd Week: Infectious Bronchitis (IB) — Eye/nasal drop (O/N).
3rd Week: Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD / Gumboro) — Eye/nasal drop (O/N).
4th-6th Week: RD La Sota booster (drinking water) and Fowl Pox (wing web puncture at 6-9 weeks).
